reading.title: The Social Side of Laughter
reading.intro_zh: 这篇短文谈“笑”的社会功能：为什么我们和别人在一起时更容易笑，以及自然的笑和刻意的笑有什么不同。内容改编自权威来源 Trends in Cognitive Sciences 期刊论文《The Social Life of Laughter》（经 NIH 旗下 PMC 收录）。

source.title: The Social Life of Laughter
source.publisher: Trends in Cognitive Sciences (PMC, National Library of Medicine / NIH)

passage: Most of us assume that laughter is simply our reaction to something funny, yet researchers who study it tell a more surprising story. Careful observation of everyday conversation reveals that comparatively little of our laughter is actually prompted by jokes; far more of it bubbles up around ordinary remarks and shared moments. Strikingly, the person who is speaking tends to laugh even more often than the person listening, which suggests that laughter is not merely an involuntary response but a deliberate signal we send to others. We are roughly thirty times more likely to laugh in the company of other people than when we are entirely alone, and the sound is so contagious that simply hearing someone else chuckle can set us off.

Scientists therefore regard laughter primarily as a social tool, a vocal gesture that establishes and strengthens the bonds between us in ways that words alone cannot. They also distinguish between two kinds: the spontaneous, involuntary laughter that erupts when we are genuinely tickled or delighted, and the controlled, voluntary laughter we produce on purpose to smooth a conversation. Brain-imaging studies show that these two varieties even engage different neural circuits. Crucially, this research reframes how we should interpret an audience that breaks into laughter. When listeners laugh along with a confident speaker, they are usually expressing warmth, connection, and shared enjoyment rather than mockery. To laugh with someone, then, is one of our oldest and most powerful ways of saying that we belong together.

questions.question: What is the main point the passage makes about laughter?
options: Laughter is mainly a social signal that connects people, not just a reaction to jokes.
People laugh only when they hear a genuinely clever joke.
Laughter is impossible to study scientifically.
Listeners always laugh more than the speaker does.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文的核心是：笑主要是一种把人联系在一起的社会信号，而不只是对笑话的反应。其余选项都与文意相反或片面。

questions.question: According to the passage, who tends to laugh more often in conversation?
options: The person who is listening.
Only people who are alone.
The person who is speaking.
Nobody laughs during ordinary conversation.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文明确说 the person who is speaking tends to laugh even more often than the person listening。

questions.question: Why does the passage say laughter is described as contagious?
options: Because jokes spread quickly from one class to another.
Because simply hearing someone else laugh can make us laugh too.
Because laughter causes illness in large crowds.
Because people laugh more when they are completely alone.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中说 the sound is so contagious that simply hearing someone else chuckle can set us off，即听到别人笑就会引发我们笑。

questions.question: What can we infer about an audience that laughs along with a confident speaker?
options: They are probably bored and want the speech to end.
They are most likely mocking the speaker in secret.
They have failed to understand the speaker at all.
They are most likely showing warmth and shared enjoyment, not mockery.
questions.explanation_zh: 末段指出，当听众和有自信的讲者一起笑时，通常是在表达温暖、连接与共同的快乐，而不是嘲笑。

questions.question: In this passage, the word "spontaneous" most nearly means
options: carefully planned in advance.
happening naturally and without being forced.
loud and unpleasant.
completely silent.
questions.explanation_zh: spontaneous 在文中与 controlled, voluntary 相对，指自然地、不受刻意控制地发生，所以选 happening naturally and without being forced。

writing.intro_zh: 今天抓五个 Lesson 63 的高价值句式，并把语境升级到更抽象的 B2+ 表达：用 admire ... for ... 写欣赏的深层原因，用 asked ... to make a speech 写正式邀请，用 This is the sort of thing that ... 写某人投入的一类活动，用 As soon as ... had finished 写完成后立即引发的连锁反应，用 To his surprise 写认知被颠覆的意外发现。

patterns.title: admire ... for ...
patterns.source: Everybody admires him for his great sense of humour.
patterns.focus_zh: admire ... for ... 用来写“因为某个原因而欣赏某人”，for 后面说明具体原因。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写人们之所以欣赏某位讲者，不是因为他的笑话本身，而是因为他能让全场观众放松并产生连接。
patterns.sample: Audiences admire her not for her jokes but for the warmth and connection she creates with everyone in the room.
patterns.tip_zh: admire 后面接人，for 后面接原因；试着把原因写成抽象品质，如 warmth, connection, sincerity 而不只是 funny。

patterns.title: asked ... to make a speech
patterns.source: One of Jeremy's closest friends asked him to make a speech.
patterns.focus_zh: asked someone to do something 写“请某人做某事”；to make a speech 表示请某人讲话或做演讲。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写组织者郑重地请一位平时怕在众人面前讲话的人发言，并解释他们为什么相信他能做到。
patterns.sample: The organisers asked the nervous young researcher to make a speech, convinced that his honesty would move the audience more than confidence ever could.
patterns.tip_zh: asked 后面先写被邀请的人，再用 to make a speech 写任务；可以加一个从句解释邀请背后的理由。

patterns.title: This is the sort of thing that ...
patterns.source: This is the sort of thing that Jeremy loves.
patterns.focus_zh: This is the sort of thing that ... 可以写某人喜欢、害怕或擅长的一类活动。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：用这个句式写公开演讲这类既让人紧张、又能带来深度满足感的事，并点出它为什么值得反复练习。
patterns.sample: Public speaking is exactly the sort of thing that terrifies people at first yet rewards them with confidence once they keep practising.
patterns.tip_zh: thing 后面的 that 从句要说明这类事对人意味着什么；试着同时点出它的难处和回报。

patterns.title: As soon as ... had finished, ...
patterns.source: As soon as he had finished, Jenny told him she wanted to go home.
patterns.focus_zh: As soon as ... had finished 写“刚刚完成某事，另一件事马上发生”，能让故事转折更清楚。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写讲者刚结束发言，全场就爆发出温暖的掌声与笑声，让他第一次意识到观众一直站在他这边。
patterns.sample: As soon as the speaker had finished, the whole hall broke into warm applause and laughter, and he finally realised the audience had been with him all along.
patterns.tip_zh: As soon as 放句首；had finished 前面要有主语，逗号后写紧接着发生的连锁反应。

patterns.title: To his surprise, ...
patterns.source: To his surprise, she said she hadn't.
patterns.focus_zh: To his surprise 用来引出“让他没想到的是”，适合写误会被解开或答案出乎意料。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一个人原本确信观众在嘲笑自己，后来才发现那笑声其实是友善的认可，彻底颠覆了他的判断。
patterns.sample: To his surprise, the laughter he had taken as mockery turned out to be a sign of genuine affection that completely changed how he saw the evening.
patterns.tip_zh: 逗号后写真正让人意外、甚至颠覆原有判断的结果；不要只写普通动作。
